title: North Vector Dynamics deep-dossier organization refresh

selectedGap.reason: The operator explicitly scoped this run to increase reviewable Canadian company coverage while preserving evidence and duplicate controls.

guardrailNotes: Private Admin Review material only. This refresh never accepts, publishes, or writes into canonical organization, capability, relationship, program, source, or evidence tables.
The existing published North Vector Dynamics record is the intentional sole duplicate match; all operations are additive or update an existing child in place, preserving stable IDs and slugs.
Company, government, investor, parliamentary, and reputable-industry sources are kept distinct. Social and uncorroborated financing claims remain discovery-only and are not candidate fields.

DRDC work is described as public research activity, the DND contribution as concept-development funding, and the MIL-V connection as prototype integration. None establishes procurement eligibility, a customer relationship, operational adoption, or classified demand.

candidates.reviewerRationale: North Vector Dynamics is already published, but its record has only the CM-70 capability and an IDEaS contribution relationship. The company now has current, concrete product pages for CI-60 counter-UAS, CI-60 Target, and SHIELD, as well as a fuller CM-70 specification. Its company announcement, a 2025 parliamentary submission, and CityNews support a bounded four-year C$4.2M DRDC hypersonic-propulsion research contract. ONE9's official portfolio and North Vector's announcement support a founding-investor relationship; Ottawa Business Journal supports a separate Convergence MIL-V prototype-integration relationship. The candidate preserves the existing organization and CM-70 IDs, adds only source-backed operations, and keeps dated, ambiguous, or discovery-only claims out of canonical fields.
reviewWarnings: North Vector's current CM-70 page lists 3 kg, 0.9 m, 3.5 km, and 900 km/h, while a dated May 2026 Janes article reports earlier 2 kg, 0.72 m, and greater-than-1,000 km/h figures. The proposed specifications use the current official page and retain the discrepancy for review.

Tech Horizons and CSG financing appears in secondary and LinkedIn discovery material, but no durable company or investor source was recovered in this run. No financing field or relationship is proposed.
ARCTOS is marked coming soon on the official site and has no concrete public specifications. It is deliberately not added as a capability.
Ottawa Business Journal documents a MIL-V prototype integration with Convergence Design Services; it is not evidence of a Canadian Armed Forces procurement, contract, or operational deployment.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: North Vector's official profile states that it is a Calgary, Canadian-owned and controlled defence technology company specializing in precision interception, autonomy, and advanced propulsion, with work from counter-UAS solutions to hypersonics.
North Vector's official company page publishes a general contact email address and telephone number for inquiries and media requests.
North Vector says DRDC awarded it a four-year C$4.2M contract to advance propulsion and hypersonic technologies, while its current product pages identify a broader counter-UAS portfolio.

The Government of Canada contribution record identifies an IDEaS Concept Development project, amount, dates, legal recipient, and desired counter-UAS outcomes, but it does not establish procurement or operational adoption.

The current CM-70 page lists 3 kg mass, 0.9 m length, 3.5 km range, 900 km/h speed, semi-active laser guidance, a forward-fragmentation warhead, and ground, vehicle, or airborne launch configurations.

North Vector describes CI-60 counter-UAS as a 0.8 kg electric, compact-lifting-body interceptor with a 2 km published range, onboard AI and near-IR guidance, field-assembled rail launch, and a Class I drone focus.

North Vector describes CI-60 Target as a 0.7 kg aerial target with a 6 km published range, programmable missions, threat-representative drone profiles, and field-assembled rail launch for SHORAD and counter-UAS training.

North Vector describes SHIELD as a modular VTOL counter-UAS system with hybrid-electric propulsion, EO/IR sensing and laser designation, airborne detection and tracking, 5-plus-hour endurance, and 40 km telemetry range.
North Vector's official announcement says DRDC awarded it a four-year C$4.2M contract to advance propulsion and hypersonic technologies.
CityNews reports that North Vector will partner with DRDC to design and test propulsion concepts for vehicles capable of travelling above Mach 5 under a C$4.2M federal contract.
North Vector's May 2025 release says ONE9 is a founding investor that helped shape the company's mission and market entry.
ONE9's current venture portfolio lists North Vector Dynamics and describes it as developing advanced and cost-effective counter-uncrewed aerial systems solutions.
Ottawa Business Journal reports that North Vector was one of Convergence's MIL-V partners and supplied a precision-guided missile for the prototype vehicle.
